newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Copper premiums fall, aluminium up.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Copper premiums fall, aluminium up.

text.p: Taipei base metal traders said on Tuesday that Taiwan's third-quarter aluminium premiums had settled higher, while rising world copper futures prices had pushed copper import premiums lower.
Traders said Taiwan's third-quarter aluminium import premiums, for general buyers, were settled at US$90 to $95 per tonne over LME futures prices, up from US$84 to $89 in the second quarter.
Premiums for few large aluminium buyers were quoted at around US$85 to $90 per tonne, traders said.
Taiwan aluminium ingots prices, despite the rising import premium, fell about US$1 as the third-quarter premium were settled below the US$95 to US$100 that buyers had anticipated.

Taiwan copper import premiums were at US$57 to US$62 per tonne over LME cash prices, down from US$60 to US$65 per tonne two weeks ago, as buying interest remained sluggish amid a recent copper futures rally, metals traders said.
"Copper premiums are falling because buyers weren't buying," a metal trader said.
World copper futures prices are now holding at pre-Sumitomo June 1996 crash levels.
Traders said local copper wire and strip prices nevertheless had risen to reflect rising world copper futures prices.
